title: Kernel Sweeper: Latency-tail-aware Autotuner for Architecture and Seq-len Profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a production-grade autotuner that continuously selects the best kernel implementation per model and request-profile, with explicit handling for architecture heterogeneity (A100/A800/H100/GPU-class variants) and sequence-length buckets. The tuner must treat prefill and decode phases separately, optimize for tail latency (99.9th percentile) under mixed loads, and provide safe fallback and rollouts. The output should be a lightweight policy that the serving runtime can consult with <1ms overhead per decision.
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner produces a kernel policy file that maps (model, arch-class, seq-len-bucket, phase) -> kernel variant and confidence score.
End-to-end 99.9th percentile latency improves by at least 15% on mixed throughput workloads compared to baseline static kernel mapping in internal benchmark (same cost).
Runtime decision latency < 1ms and memory overhead < 8MB per instance.
Graceful rollback: policy changes are canaried; any policy that increases observed error rate or tail latency by >10% in 10-minute window is automatically reverted.
Integration tests cover prefill/decode divergence and quantized kernel fallbacks.
Documentation and runbook for tuning thresholds and adding new kernel fingerprints are published in Confluence.
tasks: Design kernel fingerprint and feature vector (arch, sm_version, free_mem_pct, seq_len, batch_size, quant_mode, temperature) - Maya/Diego
Implement offline microbench harness to collect per-kernel cost surface for seq-len buckets - Diego
Prototype online lightweight bandit that prefers low-tail-latency kernels while exploring uncertain buckets - Diego
Integrate policy storage and rollout hooks into control plane (console rollouts) - Platform Team PR
Add telemetry slices to Console (per-kernel latency histograms, decision coverage) - Observability
End-to-end benchmark run and comparison vs static mapping - Performance QA
Prepare runbook and docs for customer support - SRE/Docs
notes: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after perf review; identified seq-len skew during service spikes that existing heuristic doesn't handle.

2026-02-26: Architecture meeting - agreed to split prefill and decode phases. Prefill optimization should favor throughput/occupancy-friendly kernels; decode should optimize for single-request latency and KV cache reuse. (notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/KernelSweeperDraft)

2026-03-02: Prototype microbench run on A100/A800 shows flash-attn variant reduces median but increases 99.9th by ~25% for short-decode (1-8 tokens) due to SM occupancy cliffs. Decision: include occupancy and cold-cache penalty in cost model.
2026-03-04: Diego submitted initial PR for offline profiler: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4120. Needs review for safe concurrency and profiling noise filtering.

2026-03-06: Review feedback from Priya (Perf): prefer bootstrapped confidence intervals and exponential decay window for online metrics to avoid transient flips. Also suggested a minimum exploration budget per new kernel fingerprint.
2026-03-09: Implemented online bandit (epsilon-adaptive) with tail-aware reward: reward = -alpha * p99_latency - beta * mean_cost. Tuned alpha/beta in config; default alpha=0.7, beta=0.3.

2026-03-10: Observability spike: telemetry shows increased scheduling jitter when decisions evaluated synchronously. Mitigation: move decision path to async fast-path with cached last-decision and background refresh (target stale window 3s).
2026-03-12: Security review noted need to sanitize kernel fingerprint inputs to avoid leaking host-level metrics to policy store. Added ACL and hashing step in policy key generation.

2026-03-14: Performance QA running long tail benchmark on mixed-traffic replay (20M requests). Early results: 11% p99.9 improvement; still chasing another 4% to meet goal. Next steps: tighten seq-len bucketing and enable quantized-kernel probe for small batches.
decisions: Split decision logic for prefill vs decode phases; separate cost models and exploration schedules.
Use bucketized sequence-length feature (0-8,9-32,33-128,129-512,>512) to limit policy cardinality.
Maintain a small offline profiled cost surface and reconcile online bandit updates to that surface to reduce noise.
Async decision path with cached policy entry and background refresh to eliminate per-request blocking.
Rollouts through Console's canary mechanism with automatic rollback based on latency/error SLOs.
Require a minimum exploration budget (3 minutes per new kernel fingerprint) before the tuner increases preference confidence.
risks: Exploration could increase tail latency if not heavily constrained; mitigated by strict guardrails and canary thresholds.
Profiling noise on heterogeneous hardware (different PCI-e topologies) might mislabel fast kernels as slow. Need to tag profiled runs with topology metadata.
Policy explosion if too many dimensions (model checkpoint id, tokenizer config) are included; we'll restrict keys to stable model hash + controlled runtime features.
Telemetry volume and dashboard cost — adding per-kernel p99 histograms increases storage. We'll sample and aggregate to hourly for older data.
